evidence.quote: First, HumanEval contains only 164 problems, so small differences in accuracy are inherently noisy.

The K-step unrolling training pipeline requires K+1 sequential forward passes through the backbone per training iteration (one warmup pass plus K unrolled steps), compared to a single forward pass in standard dLLM training.
At inference time, each denoising step requires executing the Mixer, Updater, and Injector in addition to the frozen backbone forward pass.
Furthermore, maintaining the constant-size persistent state tensor increases peak memory usage during generation.
Curriculum-based K scheduling or auxiliary objectives that explicitly encourage long-horizon state stability may also help close the training-to-inference extrapolation gap.
